content: I want to add distributed tracing across our service mesh. We have Prometheus for metrics and Loki for logs but no trace propagation — when something goes wrong we're stitching together logs from six services by timestamp and request ID.

OpenTelemetry would be the standard choice. You'd instrument each service with the OTEL SDK, propagate trace context via HTTP headers (W3C traceparent), and export spans to a collector that stores them in Jaeger or Tempo.

We already have Grafana so Tempo makes sense — keeps everything in one stack. The thing is, I want trace context to flow through Kafka too, not just synchronous HTTP calls. When service A publishes an event and service B consumes it, I want those to show up as part of the same trace.

You'd inject the trace context into the Kafka message headers when producing, then extract it when consuming to continue the trace. The OTEL Kafka instrumentation libraries handle this for both Go and Python.
Perfect. And I want to correlate traces with our Prometheus metrics — exemplars, right? So when I see a latency spike in Grafana I can click through to the specific traces that caused it.

Exactly. Prometheus exemplars attach trace IDs to metric observations. When you view a histogram in Grafana, exemplar dots appear that link directly to Tempo traces. It's the missing link between metrics and traces.

Fundamentally the observability stack should tell a story — metrics say something is wrong, traces show where, logs explain why. We have two out of three and traces are the gap. I'm going to prioritize this for the next quarter.
